clue.text: Cross empty gallery to take seat

indicators.note: the emptied gallery takes the next piece inside it
an empty word keeps only its shell, the outer letters of gallery

parts.note: the rump is the seat, the backside

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk across a deserted gallery and sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is the adjective (bad-tempered), not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for someone irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Frolic in punt, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word said aloud is a soundalike of the one entered

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a gamble

explanation.surface: Larking about in a flat-bottomed boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the boat; here it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to frolic is to skip and leap playfully.

clue.text: Alarming seeing one in gents put out

indicators.note: put out here signals the letters are thrown out of order, so the pool is shuffled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled by a stranger in the gents being ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like a phrase meaning upset; 'put' is fodder and 'out' the signal to rearrange GENTS with I and PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something alarming is disturbing and distressing.

clue.text: Unattractively artificial snap capturing conclusion

indicators.note: the photo holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, a pic
the conclusion is the last part

explanation.surface: A photo that captures an ending looks fake and unappealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as a descriptive word means synthetic and fake in an off-putting way.

clue.text: Perfect female, wild

parts.note: wild, ungoverned, means lawless

explanation.surface: A description of an ideal woman as untamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: perfect means without any defect or fault.

clue.text: Look, a new mortgage?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out a fresh home financing deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a mortgage is one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is an example: money borrowed against property.

clue.text: Closest direction to circle inlet

indicators.note: the direction surrounds the next piece

parts.note: west is a compass direction
an arm of the sea is an inlet

explanation.surface: Directions to the nearest way round a small bay.
explanation.walkthrough: In hide-and-seek, someone near the hidden thing is told they are getting warmer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a searching game, 'hot' and 'warm' mean near; so this superlative means nearest.

clue.text: Lug around say, turning impatient

indicators.note: the ear goes around the next piece

parts.note: lug is slang for an ear

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means say, for example

explanation.surface: Someone lugging a load round, growing impatient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is the noun (an ear), not the verb carry; 'turning' makes GE from EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: keen and impatient to get going.

clue.text: Wicked lapse is end, almost

parts.note: a moral lapse is a sin

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for end

parts.note: a term is an end, a limit

explanation.surface: A moral failing is nearly over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: evil, menacing and malevolent.

clue.text: Lose track of dispatch on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the M1 is the main motorway, written MI in crosswords
to dispatch is to kill, to slay

explanation.surface: Losing your way while dispatching goods on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to misplace something is to lose track of it.

clue.text: Salt rib concerned with seasoning

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, a tar
to rib is to tease, to rag
on means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: Salting and flavouring a rib of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' and 'rib' look culinary but are a sailor and a verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an aromatic herb used to flavour food.

clue.text: Appealing with turn to bat

parts.note: an inning is a turn at batting, in baseball

explanation.surface: A batsman's charm when it is his go at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a winning smile is charming and attractive.

clue.text: Proust, it gets translated better

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A claim that Proust improves in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb (surpass), not the comparative it reads as.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to outdo or surpass someone is to do better than them.

clue.text: Bride bristled accepting rubbish

indicators.note: the two words take in the run of letters that spans them

explanation.surface: A bride bristles at having to take something worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: scattered waste or refuse.

clue.text: Calm about beginning to locate cut

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the first letter of locate is taken

parts.note: axed means cut, scrapped

explanation.surface: Staying calm about a slashed budget at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: at ease, unruffled and composed.

clue.text: Stolen cabinet is damaged, for sure

indicators.note: a damaged thing is broken up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A burglary report: the stolen cabinet has certainly been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute is certain, true for sure.

clue.text: Tower guard's exploit with sweetheart consumed by drink

indicators.note: the drink takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: beer is a drink
the heart of sweet is its middle letter
an exploit is a feat

explanation.surface: A Tower of London guard's sweetheart and a heroic deed drowned in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeomen Warders who guard the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular name for the ceremonial guards of the Tower of London.

clue.text: Expert reportedly beat golfer's measure of skill

indicators.note: the word said aloud only sounds like the letters entered

parts.note: handy means expert, skilful
to cap is to beat, outdo

explanation.surface: A golf pro's rating is said to be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, the number of strokes allowed reflects a player's ability.

clue.text: Opinionated and terribly vague trite man

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Describing a dull, opinionated man who spouts clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: fond of disputing and quarrelsome in views.

clue.text: Insanity of crowd welcoming danger, oddly

indicators.note: the crowd takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of danger are taken

explanation.surface: The madness of a crowd that embraces danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: lunacy, mental derangement.

clue.text: Playing oldies I love

indicators.note: letters at play are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan who adores spinning old records.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to adore and worship.

clue.text: Strangely, dog in street ultimately ate dull food

indicators.note: the jumbled dog goes inside the other pieces
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of ate is used
strangely rearranged letters of dog

explanation.surface: A stray dog in the street eats something bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling and unexciting food.

clue.text: Do translation of French mock exam's opening

parts.note: de is French for of
cod means mock or fake

indicators.note: an opening is the start of something, so only the first letter of exam is used

explanation.surface: Translating a French practice exam's introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mock exam' is a practice paper in British schools; here 'mock' is COD (fake).
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher something is to translate it from a code.

clue.text: Seat could help an individual rest initially

indicators.note: the first letters of the five words are taken

explanation.surface: A seat might help someone take a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a seat for one person with a back.

clue.text: Stand without warning shout and put wood back?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stand surrounds the shout

parts.note: a stand is a rest, a support
fore is the golfer's warning cry

explanation.surface: Stand still without warning and put wood back.
explanation.definitionFit: To replant trees on cleared land is to restore the woodland.

clue.text: Company's time leads to charge

parts.note: CO is company, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A firm's timetable that results in a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a price or fee.

clue.text: Escort man working to protect Queen

indicators.note: the outer pieces wrap around the queen

parts.note: a chap is a man
on means working, functioning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A bodyguard on duty protecting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and supervises a young person, an escort.

clue.text: Rewarding, if tedious, to keep skilful

indicators.note: the words keep the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Work that pays though dull still keeps a talented person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: talented and very able.

clue.text: It's standard having a lot put on tick?

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: par is a standard level
a lot is a plot of land, a site

explanation.surface: A standard plot marked with a tick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' is the bloodsucking creature, not the mark; the question mark shows it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is an example of an organism living off a host.

clue.text: Catches vehicle finally, the final vehicle?

parts.note: to catch words is to hear them

indicators.note: the last letter of vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone catching a bus at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a whimsical definition: the car in which one takes a last ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral car carries the deceased on their last journey.
